subject: Operational leeway and monthly credit framework for SLA
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Paul Reiner <paul@marigoldhealth.com>
Cc: Sam Bhatt <sam.bhatt@marigoldhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Operational leeway and monthly credit framework for SLA

Hi Paul / Sam,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great to see Marigold moving toward production. I wanted to follow up with a concrete proposal so we can align on SLA mechanics without blocking your launch. High level: we can keep our standard availability commitment (99.9% monthly) but introduce a narrow operational "leeway" for known batched-inference tail events and autoscaling warmups, paired with a clear monthly credit framework.

Key points in the proposal (attached: marigold-draft-sla-exception-v1.pdf; analysis attached as latency-analysis-sep-2026.csv):
- Availability baseline: Redwood standard 99.9% monthly uptime remains the target.
- Operational leeway: carveout for transient latency spikes caused by autoscaling warmups or cold-starts and for brief large-batch backfills. This would be limited to X warmup windows per region and capped at 6 hours/month aggregated across your account.
- Credit tiers (monthly invoice credit):
  * 99.5% - 99.9% => 5% credit
  * 99.0% - 99.5% => 12% credit
  * <99.0% => 30% credit
- Latency SLOs (informational): p95 < 180ms, p99 < 600ms for steady-state requests. Credits remain tied to availability (uptime), not latency, to avoid double-counting.
- Measurement & reporting: UTC monthly windows; Redwood provides raw signal and a short remediation report within 5 business days when credits are triggered.
- Caps & protections: monthly credit cap at 20% of invoice in the pilot phase; credits issued as bill credit (applied next invoice).

As you mentioned, your Nov 15 rollout timeline is tight — if this framework looks acceptable we can spin up a 30-day pilot and include the exception language as a short addendum to the master contract.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call today or tomorrow to walk the draft? If you prefer, I can loop in Marisa from Legal and Kim from Engineering to tighten language on warmups and the technical caps.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: marigold-draft-sla-exception-v1.pdf (draft SLA addendum), latency-analysis-sep-2026.csv (sample metrics)
From: Paul Reiner <paul@marigoldhealth.com>

Cc: Sam Bhatt <sam.bhatt@marigoldhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational leeway and monthly credit framework for SLA

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the attachments. A couple quick clarifications before we loop legal:
1) Measurement window — you say UTC monthly windows. For our reporting and budget planning we need the precise measurement cadence (are credits computed from a rolling 30-day window or calendar month?).
2) Warmup carveout — we understand autoscaling spikes, but we can't have unlimited or vaguely-defined "warmup" exemptions. Can you specify what constitutes a warmup event (e.g., <15 minutes per newly provisioned instance) and whether the cap is per-region or global?
3) Credit type — we want credits to be applied as invoice-level bill credits (not refunds) and the cap needs to be explicit. The 20% cap in pilot sounds reasonable but we may need to scale after the pilot if we see patterned behavior.

We are on a tight timeline: if we can get language locked by EOD Friday (10/30) we can stay on track for Nov 15. I can join a call at 1:30pm PT today.

-Paul

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Jordan / Kim —

Thanks for the ping — I reviewed Paul's points and attached a one-page addendum draft (marigold-draft-sla-exception-v1.pdf) that aims to be narrow and customer-friendly while protecting Redwood. Summary of changes and our recommendations:

1) Measurement window: credits will be calculated on a calendar-month basis (UTC) using Redwood's availability signal. We'll include a short reconciliation process: Redwood provides raw minute-level availability for the window and Marigold has 5 business days to request audit if they dispute the calculation.

2) Warmup carveout: defined as "Transient performance deviations up to 15 minutes per newly provisioned inference instance during autoscaling events, aggregated across regions; cap 6 hours per calendar month, account-level." This keeps the exception measurable and limited. Engineering confirm please.

3) Credit mechanics: pilot credit tiers as Jordan outlined, with a monthly cap equal to 20% of the billed invoice for that calendar month. Credits are issued as invoice-level bill credits applied to the following invoice cycle. If monthly usage increases materially during pilot, parties will revisit the cap in good faith.

4) Latency: we will treat latency metrics as operational observability only (p95/p99) — they won't independently trigger credits to avoid overlapping remedy paths.

5) Pilot & termination: pilot begins on deployment date (agreed as Nov 15) for 90 days; either party can propose adjustments after the pilot.

Next steps: Jordan — get Paul's confirmation on the calendar-month measurement and the warmup definition. Kim — please confirm the 15-minute / 6-hour cap is implementable from the runtime/telemetry side and that Redwood can generate the raw minute-level availability report as described.

If everyone is ok, I'll finalize the PDF and send to Paul for signature (DocuSign link will be included).

Best,
